content.p: On the evening of 29 May 2022, the Punjabi singer and politician Sidhu Moose Wala was shot dead in his vehicle near Jawaharke, a village in Mansa district of Punjab, a day after the state government reduced his security. He was 28, according to the BBC. His death provoked national outrage and a political storm over the withdrawal of his guards.

Punjab Police say the killing was carried out by the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, and Goldy Brar, a Canada-based gangster, claimed responsibility; reports differ on whether the police charge sheet names him or Bishnoi as the mastermind. More than 30 people have been accused, and four of them have been killed, two in police encounters and two in jail. Everyone named here is accused, and no conviction is reported in the sources. The trial in Mansa has moved slowly, and Brar had not been arrested in the latest reports.

Moose Wala was driving his Mahindra Thar on a road in Jawaharke with two companions, a friend and a cousin, when the vehicle was waylaid and fired on by six shooters, according to The Tribune. A CCTV clip circulated on social media showing a car following his vehicle, and another stopping in front of it, after which firing began, according to the first information report as described by Deccan Herald. The post-mortem report, quoted by Gulf News, recorded 19 bullet injuries and said he died within 15 minutes of being shot. The two companions survived with injuries, India TV reported.

The day before, the Punjab government had scaled back his protection, the BBC said. Police told the BBC that his guard had been reduced from four commandos to two, and that those two were not with him when he was attacked. He was one of more than 400 people in Punjab whose security detail had been withdrawn or reduced. Opposition leaders asked why the cover was cut, and Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann ordered an inquiry led by a high court judge.

That same evening a Canada-based gangster, Goldy Brar, reportedly claimed responsibility in a Facebook post, Gulf News reported, and he was described as a close associate of Lawrence Bishnoi. Punjab's police chief, VK Bhawra, said on the Sunday that a Canada-based gangster had claimed responsibility. The family asked him for an apology for linking the death to gang rivalry before an investigation had been completed. On the Monday Bhawra clarified that he had not called Moose Wala a gangster or someone affiliated with gangsters. He said "One Goldy Brar has claimed the responsibility on behalf of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang" and that he had been "misquoted" by some media outlets.

Police said the killing appeared to be retaliation for the 2021 murder of Vicky Middukhera, a Youth Akali Dal leader. According to Deccan Herald, the name of Moose Wala's manager, Shaganpreet, had figured in the Middukhera case, and police said he had fled to Australia. This is the police account of the motive.

The first arrest came on 31 May 2022, when police detained Manpreet Singh and accused him of supplying vehicles to the attackers. Gulf News reported that he was reportedly trying to hide among pilgrims in Uttarakhand and was believed to have given key logistical support. A third man, Davinder Singh, known as Kala, was arrested on 5 June in Haryana, and two suspects were said to have stayed with him. Lawrence Bishnoi, who was already in jail, was arrested by the Punjab police in the case, Outlook said. He told Delhi Police about arms suppliers' hideouts across several states, Gulf News reported.

The gangsters Jagroop Singh Rupa and Manpreet Singh, alias Manu Kusa, who were among the accused, died in a police encounter in Amritsar district. Two other accused, Mandeep Singh, alias Toofan, and Mohan Singh, were murdered in the Goindwal Jail in Tarn Taran district, according to The Tribune.

On 26 August 2022 Mansa police filed a 1,850-page charge sheet in the Mansa court. It named 24 accused: 20 arrested and four abroad, Goldy Brar, Sachin Thapan, Anmol Bishnoi, the brother of Lawrence Bishnoi, and Lipin Nehra. The Mansa police chief, Gaurav Toora, said 36 people had been booked and that eight were still out of custody. The Indo-Canadian Voice, citing IANS, wrote that 36 people were named in the charge sheet. It listed 122 witnesses, including eyewitnesses, friends who were with Moose Wala, doctors and hotel staff, and forensic reports, CCTV footage and recovered weapons as evidence.

Reports differ on who the charge sheet calls the mastermind. IANS said it named Lawrence Bishnoi as the main mastermind and listed a Canada-based gangster, reportedly a Bishnoi gang member who had already claimed responsibility. Outlook, writing in 2024, said the charge sheet describes Brar as the mastermind, acting to "avenge" Middukhera's killing. The Special Investigation Team's chief, Pramod Ban, said Bishnoi had confessed that the plan was hatched in August 2021 to avenge Middukhera's death. Outlook, citing the charge sheet, said Brar worked out the plan together with seven named co-accused, including Lawrence Bishnoi, Anmol Bishnoi and Pawan Bishnoi, and with the shooters. Police said they would start extradition for the gangsters abroad.

On 26 July 2023 the chief judicial magistrate in Mansa committed the case to the sessions court, because it could be tried only there. By then 29 people had been arrested, and Brar, Nehra, Anmol Bishnoi and Sachin Thapan were still abroad, The Tribune reported.

On 1 May 2024 District Sessions Judge H S Grewal framed charges against Lawrence Bishnoi and 26 others, including murder, attempt to murder, rioting with a deadly weapon, destruction of evidence, harbouring offenders and criminal conspiracy under the Indian Penal Code, along with Arms Act offences. The family's lawyer said the court dismissed the discharge applications of Bishnoi, Bhagwanpuria, Jagtar Singh and Charanjit Singh Chetan. Moose Wala's father, Balkaur Singh, said the family was feeling some relief for the first time in 24 months. Brar, the prime accused, had not been arrested and no charges had been framed against him, according to Outlook, which also said that the Government of India had designated him a terrorist under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act in January 2024.

The trial has since moved in short steps. Two eyewitnesses, Gurpreet Singh and Gurvinder Singh, were reported to have identified the shooters, the weapons and the vehicles in court. The first investigating officer, Angrez Singh, died on 23 May 2025 before he could testify. In September 2025 Balkaur Singh asked the court to have the accused brought in person rather than by video link, because his eyesight was weak, and the court agreed. On 16 January 2026 an official witness gave only part of his evidence, since the defence lawyer for Lawrence Bishnoi and Bhagwanpuria did not attend, and the court fixed 6 February for the rest. India TV reported on 12 March 2026 that the Supreme Court had granted bail to Pawan Bishnoi and Jagtar Singh, who it said had been in custody for more than three years.

Goldy Brar, whose full name is Satinderjeet Singh, was added by India's Home Ministry to its list of designated terrorists in January 2024, Daily Pioneer reported. It said Interpol issued a Red Notice in 2022 and the National Investigation Agency offered a reward of 10 lakh rupees and charge-sheeted him in cases including Moose Wala's killing. The FBI has since placed him on its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list, and a US federal warrant issued in Los Angeles names him as the alleged North American head of the Lawrence Bishnoi group, charging racketeering, extortion and drug conspiracies. Those US allegations are separate from the Mansa case.
